messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] INLA stable version change since last week?
parts:
Can u send me code++ so I can rerun it here?

Sent from my iPhone

On 8 Feb 2019, at 03:00, mikefa...@gmail.com wrote:

Hi,

(Forgive me for not having this better documented, but I'm writing in case I'm not the only one having this problem).  

I have a model that took about a minute to run last week.   A colleague tried to run the model from a cloned repo and it crashed out.  I tried to reproduce her process on another computer, with a fresh package install, and got the same error: After hanging here:

inla_parse_INLA...
section[INLA.Parameters]
lincomb.derived.only = [Yes]
lincomb.derived.correlation.matrix = [No]
global_node.factor = 2.000
global_node.degree = 2147483647
reordering = -1
Contents of ai_param 0000000003691DD0
Optimiser: DEFAULT METHOD
Option for domin-BFGS: epsx = 0.005
Option for domin-BFGS: epsf = 1e-005 (rounding error)
Option for domin-BFGS: epsg = 0.005
Option for GSL-BFGS2: tol  = 0.1
Option for GSL-BFGS2: step_size = 1
Option for GSL-BFGS2: epsx = 0.005
Option for GSL-BFGS2: epsf = 0.000353553
Option for GSL-BFGS2: epsg = 0.005
Restart: 0
Mode known: No


it eventually crashes with

              Error in inla.inlaprogram.has.crashed() : 
  The inla-program exited with an error. Unless you interupted it yourself, please rerun with verbose=TRUE and check the output carefully



So I updated my original machine and got the same problem.  


(While I wish everything was Dockerized...) The only difference between last week and this week is fresh installs.

Anyone else having a similar problem?  It could be with a dependency, but it looks like there was some recent versions committed https://bitbucket.org/hrue/r-inla/commits/tag/Version_19.02.06.

Thanks,

--Mike

Apologies.  The problem was on my end and had to do with a misformatted data frame that I managed not to notice because a good version was loaded in the R workspace that shouldn't've been there.  I deleted the message from the group so as not to add further confusion. 

I'm relatively new to INLA, and the support you offer is amazing. Thank you,

--Mike
